comment: The manifest.json inside a .nlkbak bundle. `backup` is a v3 backup document embedded VERBATIM — byte-for-byte what the JSON exporter writes — so a v4 reader hands it to the unchanged v3 importer and a v3-only client can recover the notes by extracting this one field. `attachments` is an additive index; it never changes what `backup` means.

rules.archive: ZIP. Entries are stored (method 0) on write; a reader also accepts deflate (method 8) so a bundle re-zipped by the operating system still imports.
rules.entryNames: manifest.json at the archive root, and media/<attachmentId> for each attachment. attachmentId must match ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$, which is what makes zip-slip structurally impossible: a reader resolves media entries from the validated id in the manifest, never from a path in the archive.
rules.noteId: The note's id inside `backup.notes`. Import reassigns local ids, so a reader must map old note id -> newly assigned id and rewrite the attachment's owner accordingly.
rules.sha256: Lowercase hex of the entry's bytes. A mismatch drops that one attachment and is reported; it must never drop the note.
rules.additive: Import is additive, exactly as v3 import is: notes arrive as new notes with newly allocated ids. Importing the same bundle twice yields two copies, and the attachment ids are re-minted so the second copy does not collide with the first.
rules.excluded: A bundle never carries access tokens, refresh tokens, encryption keys, cached sessions, sync cursors, server revisions, knownCloudIds, or any owner identifier.
